source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Geography Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The Blue Planet
points: About **71%** of the Earth's surface is **water** and only **29%** is **land** — hence the "Blue Planet."
Most water is **salty ocean water**; only a small share is **fresh water** (rivers, lakes, glaciers, groundwater).
The huge water body is divided into **oceans**; the large land masses into **continents**.

sections.heading: 2. The Five Oceans (largest → smallest)
points: **Pacific Ocean** — the **largest and deepest**; contains the **Mariana Trench** (deepest point).
**Atlantic Ocean** — second largest; 'S'-shaped; busiest for trade.
**Indian Ocean** — the **only ocean named after a country (India)**.
**Southern (Antarctic) Ocean** — surrounds Antarctica.
**Arctic Ocean** — the **smallest and shallowest**, around the North Pole, largely ice-covered.

sections.heading: 3. The Seven Continents (largest → smallest)
points: **Asia** — the **largest**; has the **highest point, Mount Everest**; India lies here.
**Africa** — second largest; the **Equator, Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn all pass through it**; **Sahara** = largest hot desert; **River Nile** = longest river.
**North America** and **South America** (the Amazon river & rainforest in S. America).
**Antarctica** — around the South Pole; **coldest**, ice-covered, no permanent human population.
**Europe** — connected to Asia (together **Eurasia**).
**Australia** — the **smallest**; the only continent that is also a single country (an 'island continent').

sections.heading: 4. Continents and Oceans Together
points: The **Equator** passes through **Africa, South America and Asia** (and Australia's north).
Continents are separated (or joined) by oceans and seas; some are linked by narrow **isthmuses**.
The distribution of land and water shapes **climate, winds and ocean currents**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Water 71% : Land 29% → the Blue Planet.
Oceans (big→small): Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern > Arctic.
Pacific = largest & deepest (Mariana Trench); Arctic = smallest; Indian Ocean = named after a country.
Continents (big→small): Asia > Africa > North America > South America > Antarctica > Europe > Australia.
Highest point = Mt Everest (Asia); largest hot desert = Sahara (Africa); longest river = Nile.
Australia = smallest continent (island continent); Antarctica = coldest, uninhabited.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Pacific**, not the Atlantic, is the largest and deepest ocean.
The **Indian Ocean** is the only ocean named after a country.
**Asia** is the largest continent and **Australia** the smallest.
Africa is the continent through which **all three** — Equator and both Tropics — pass.
